title: Mechanically shaped single bones are unreliable guides to phylogenetic affinity

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Mechanically shaped single bones are unreliable guides to phylogenetic affinity

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because the form of bones such as the scapula or vertebrae reflects the mechanical stresses of an animal's mode of life, resemblance or difference in a single such bone is no reliable evidence for or against blood-relationship, as in comparing Zeuglodon with whales.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVI: On Form and Mechanical Efficiency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: That the Zeuglodon has a scapula like that of a whale is to my mind no necessary argument that he is akin by blood-relationship to a whale: that his dorsal vertebrae are very different from a whale’s is no conclusive argument that such blood-relationship is lacking.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVI, “On Form and Mechanical Efficiency”; topic “Mechanics and phylogeny”. Scope: use of skeletal characters in vertebrate phylogenetics, especially in lineages that changed habitat

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch16-17: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Predictive reliability has a direct modern metric and independent reference phylogenies reduce circularity. Large public morphology and tree databases permit a broad, standard comparative analysis now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare phylogenetic accuracy from single mechanically responsive bones against multi-character morphology and molecular reference trees, stratified by ecological convergence. Reliability is measured by topology error and support.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Choice of a “mechanically shaped” character may be partly outcome-dependent.

Fossil taxa lack molecular reference trees.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Independent trees and morphological matrices exist, so homoplasy of single bones can be compared with other characters in living vertebrates. That is a fair proxy for 'unreliable as evidence of blood-relationship'. The fossil illustration cannot be checked with molecules, and habitat-linked convergence is only partly separated from coding decisions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Using molecular or other independent trees as the reference, compare phylogenetic signal and homoplasy of scapulae and vertebrae with that of other skeletal characters, especially in lineages that changed habitat. The claim is supported if those mechanically loaded bones mislead more often than other characters; equal or higher reliability would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Extinct test cases such as Zeuglodon have no genome, so the reference tree is itself partly morphological.

Character coding and missing fossils change apparent homoplasy.
